sentence: A famous old photograph by Harold Edgerton shows a bullet going through an apple. That bullet flew at about eight hundred fifty meters a second.
claim: Edgerton's famous photograph shows a .30-calibre bullet at about 2,800 feet per second (about 850 m/s) passing through an apple.
source_title: MIT Edgerton Center (the photograph and its bullet speed; recalled, not opened; page address from memory)
note: FROM MEMORY, NOT OPENED: a person must open the Edgerton Center / MIT Museum page for the photograph and check the bullet speed (about 2,800 ft/s) and the caliber. Rifle bullets run about 700 to 1,000 m/s, so 850 m/s is typical.

sentence: The apple is about eight centimeters across. So the bullet crosses it in less than a ten-thousandth of a second.
note: DERIVATION (calc.py, run it); no outside source. Apple width (8 cm) is our assumption (typical apples are about 7 to 9 cm).

sentence: Here, that takes about one second.
note: DERIVATION (calc.py, run it); no outside source.

sentence: It's moving more than twice as fast as sound, so it drags a narrow cone of air behind it.
claim: A body moving faster than sound makes a cone-shaped shock wave (Mach cone); 850 m/s is Mach 2.5 (half-angle of the cone about 24 degrees).
source_title: OpenStax, University Physics Vol. 1, 17.8 Shock Waves (recalled, not opened)
note: FROM MEMORY, NOT OPENED (the builder recalled this; no source text was read this session); a person must open the source and check the number and the wording before posting. At 850 m/s the bullet is Mach 2.5 (calc.py), so the cone is narrow.

sentence: Even now, a table a meter wide would take it about twelve seconds to cross.
note: DERIVATION (calc.py, run it); no outside source. The 1 m table is our assumption.

sentence: In real time, that was far too quick to blink.
claim: A human blink takes roughly 100 to 400 milliseconds; the bullet crosses the apple in 94 microseconds.
note: FROM MEMORY, NOT OPENED (the builder recalled this; no source text was read this session); a person must open the source and check the number and the wording before posting. The 94 microseconds is a derivation (calc.py); the blink duration is a hedge ('roughly a tenth of a second or more').
